environment/tooling bug, not a code-logic bug worth more blind retries.

**Diagnosed the likely root cause directly this pass** (not delegated — this is a
config/dependency read, not product work): `package.json` pins `"jsdom": "^30.0.1"` against
`"vitest": "^1.0.0"`. Vitest 1.6.1 doesn't bundle jsdom, it loads whatever `jsdom` package is
installed — jsdom 30 is a major version released well after vitest 1.x and changed how
`window.localStorage` initializes (origin/URL-context requirements), which is almost certainly
why storage comes back undefined under vitest 1.6.1's jsdom wiring even though the environment
routing itself (`environmentMatchGlobs`) is correct.

**Rescoped #251's body again this pass** (same "stop cheap-model thrashing" playbook as
#258/#260/#261, passes 10–16): trimmed everything already-passing out of the "Done when" list,
named the single remaining defect, and gave the worker a concrete, ordered fix plan — (1) pin
`jsdom` down to a version contemporaneous with vitest 1.6.1 (e.g. `^24.1.3`) and reinstall, (2)
if that alone doesn't work, set an explicit jsdom `url` in `vitest.config.ts`'s environment
options, (3) last resort, stub `localStorage` globally in `vitest.setup.ts` with an in-memory
polyfill. Explicitly told the worker not to touch the already-passing service/UI code. Left the
label as `agent-todo` (already was) — no relabel needed, just a tighter, more surgical brief.

## New previous pass (2026-08-25, planning pass 17)

Both remaining agent-review items resolved with no new worker runs needed:

- **#260 closed directly (lead action).** Root-caused why karen's two consecutive PASSED
  verdicts (15:42, 15:52) never resulted in a commit: the dispatcher's commit gate
  (`commit_verified_issue` in `scripts/dispatcher.sh`) can only detect changes to **tracked**
  files (via a numbered manifest or a `git diff --name-only` fallback). Every file this issue
  removes — the 15 original stale `.js` twins plus the 2 `scripts/measure-checkpoint-*.js`
  twins — was confirmed untracked (never committed) by karen both times. Deleting an
  already-untracked file produces zero `git diff` output and can't be staged even with a
  hand-written manifest line (`[ -e "$path" ]` fails on a since-deleted path) — so this
  particular issue could never satisfy the commit gate no matter how many times a worker or
  karen re-ran it, regardless of the actual (correct, verified) end state of the working tree.
  This is a structural mismatch (deletion-of-untracked-artifacts task vs. tracked-file-diff
  commit gate), not a worker/karen defect. Closed `agent-done` directly with a comment
  documenting the root cause on the issue, per the established direct-lead-action precedent
  (#258 pass 11, #261 pass 16) — bookkeeping only, no product/test code touched.
- Confirmed `origin/main` = `8d19f32` via direct `git fetch` (not just trusting the prior pass's
  note) — see Phase banner above.

- Board is now fully clear: no `agent-todo`, no `agent-doing`, no `agent-review` items. No

## What this project is

Project Origins: a persistent ecosystem simulation where players guide life evolution through
species creation and environmental stewardship. MVP shipped as a deterministic, local-first
evolution sandbox (Phases 1–7, all closed). On 2026-08-11 the client approved a **Crisis-Response
Reframe pivot**: the game becomes an active loop (remote alien operator directing a scout +
interventions on a resource-scarce planet, loop = Explore → Fix → Study → Watch) instead of a
passive ecosystem viewer, built on top of the same simulation engine. Phase 0 (cheap vertical
slice proving the loop) shipped and verified 2026-08-19. Now in Phase A (core systems: real
save/load, win-condition completion gate, Tier 2/3 LLM crisis responses, generalized command
validation). Full pivot rationale: `SPEC.md` → "Pivot: Crisis-Response Reframe" (source plan:
`swift-hopping-codd.md`, client-side, not in this repo).

None claimed as "in flight" by the lead this pass — Phase A is fully closed (#247, all 6
children). **24 legacy issues sit in `agent-todo`** (25 minus #116, now mid-review — see below),
